ROUTE: Avocet-235B
REASON: The task demands precise extraction of structured data (price, dimensions, weight, review counts) and strict adherence to a rigid three-sentence template per item. Avocet scores significantly higher on Extraction & Retrieval (81.6 vs. 78.5), and its flat, moderation-oriented preference profile suggests it is more likely to follow formatting constraints closely rather than embellish with open-ended creative detail.

ROUTE: Lapwing-235B
REASON: This is a structured creative-generation and support-dialogue task—writing templated buyer’s-guide blurbs that require following a strict format while drawing on provided specs. Lapwing scores meaningfully higher on Creative Generation (81.2 vs. 78.8) and Support Dialogue (82.4 vs. 79.4), and its self-reported preferences strongly favor open-ended generative work, making it the better fit for producing engaging, constrained product copy. While Avocet leads in Extraction & Retrieval, the lightweight data-pulling here is straightforward and outweighed by Lapwing’s stronger generative and dialogue capabilities.

ROUTE: Lapwing-235B
REASON: This is a generative writing task (crafting product blurbs) where Lapwing shows a materially higher Creative Generation score (81.2 vs. 78.8) and self-reports strong appetite for generative work. While it requires inserting provided data points, the extraction demand is low because the user will supply labeled fields explicitly, making Lapwing’s creative strength the better match.

ROUTE: Avocet-235B
REASON: The task is heavily extraction-driven: the user will supply structured product data and requires each blurb to follow a rigid three-sentence template with specific facts (price, dimensions/weight, review count) mapped to fixed sentence roles. Avocet scores meaningfully higher on Extraction & Retrieval (81.6 vs. 78.5) and its flat preference profile fits repetitive, constrained templated generation better than Lapwing, which favors open-ended creative latitude.

ROUTE: Lapwing-235B
REASON: The task is primarily creative generation—writing templated product blurbs from structured data—and Lapwing scores meaningfully higher than Avocet on the Internal Creative Generation eval (81.2 vs. 78.8). Lapwing also self-reports the strongest preference for generative, open-ended work in the fleet, making it the natural choice for this buyer's-guide content.
